从养成到游戏性到手感都是一坨大的，但是考虑到它的属性和定价我还不好开喷 23块钱你把它当某种牛肉周边还算值得□你把它当游戏□那我的评价是vedal应该给游玩时所受的折磨支付精神损失费 很难想象作为一个2025年的游戏它没有小地图，需要你使用DNA引擎的碳基CPU构建地图；神人默认键位让我需要在紧张操作的过程中大拇指跨老远按v；新手引导缺失，你不看直播都不知道按两下T能返回到传送位置；直角般的游戏难度曲线致敬大作丝之歌，让人怀疑是不是想要用boss拖游戏进度；视角随boss乱转，让你在激烈紧张的战斗中体验主角面对强大敌人时的茫然无措；养成系统，战力全靠roll，知识的巨大消耗让我不得不捏着鼻子用一开始roll到的法术，哪怕后面遇到了我更喜欢的法术也因为加点问题不得不放弃。 总结为AI创作者做的AI般的游戏吸引一堆AI管人痴为了第二层的AI彩蛋受苦受难

初见4层boss被打飞了，我是在玩iwanna吗？（ 玩了三把来到了第三层，简单评价一下目前的感觉。事实上，很难说这个游戏是一个完整的游戏。作为一个2025年发售的rougelike游戏，你能看见： 1.没有小地图：初步体验来看，游戏和以撒的游戏类型是类似的，不理解为什么不给一个小地图。虽然事实上游戏的地图并不复杂，坚持找肯定是能找到boss房间的。但是地图可以很好的减少重复走路的时间消耗，总不能是在让我边玩边遵循广度搜索算法吧（笑 2.操作键位非常奇怪：不太懂vedal是用的哪个操作模式，个人体验来看手柄完全没法玩，键盘初始键位习惯很奇怪，不符合常规游戏的思维惯性，需要做一定的调整。比较典型的就是初始U键释放大招，很难想象人类的手指怎么在一手WASD的情况下伸出20CM的手指点U。手柄的问题巨大，右螺旋锁定敌人，左肩键攻击是什么神秘设计。 3.没有洗点：代表着你的所有强化将没有回头路可以走，一层走完你的法术基本就固定了。哪怕后面遇到了更好用的法术，强化带来的巨大知识消耗让你很难放弃手上+3+4的法术重新培养一个法术。 4.部分设计的不合理：比如我遇到了一个事件。接下来的五个房价视线受损。但是这个视线受损指的不是角色而是玩家，拥有这个诅咒的情况下我连强化法术的页面都看不齐了。第二层的boss在瞬移的时候连着玩家的视角一起拖拽，对于一个rougelike游戏，没有局外成长，没有难度选项，这代表这我完成了一把游戏后对于下一把游戏没有任何除了技术提升外的帮助，加上较高的难度使得我没有那么大的兴趣重复死亡过程。 5.对了，差点忘记中文翻译的传统口口口问题，对于中英文的逗号忘记做翻译导致显示错误。 6.为什么水晶房间给的遗物不能放弃，谁懂硬塞一个玻璃眼和玻璃拐杖5血瞬间暴毙的救赎感噶人们。 暂时遇到了这些问题，以后遇到了再写，当支持Vedal游戏了，但是真的很难说这是一款出色的游戏。感觉还是一个未完成品，期待后续更新吧。还有真的有人肘赢了四层boss吗？ After three runs and making it to the third floor (and just getting wrecked by my first encounter with the Floor 4 boss—am I playing some kind of I Wanna Be the Guy fangame?), here are my initial thoughts. Honestly, it's hard to call this a fully polished game. For a roguelike released in 2025, here are some noticeable issues: No Minimap: The gameplay feels similar to The Binding of Isaac, so it's confusing why there's no minimap. While the layout isn't overly complex and you can eventually find the boss room through persistence, a minimap would significantly reduce unnecessary backtracking. Am I really supposed to perform a breadth-first search algorithm while playing? (laughs) Awkward Control Scheme: It's unclear what control style the developer was aiming for. In my experience, the game is nearly unplayable with a controller. The default keyboard layout is also unintuitive and goes against common gaming conventions—it requires manual tweaking. A prime example is the ultimate skill bound to the U key by default. It's hard to imagine how anyone can comfortably press U while using WASD—unless they have 20cm-long fingers. Controller support is even worse: using the right stick to lock onto enemies and the left shoulder button for attack? What kind of design is that? No Respec Mechanism: This means all your upgrades are permanent. Once you finish a floor, your spell build is pretty much locked in. Even if you find a better spell later, the high Knowledge cost of upgrades makes it impractical to abandon a +3 or +4 spell to start leveling a new one from scratch. Questionable Design Choices: I encountered an event that imposed "impaired vision" for the next five rooms. But the impairment affected the player's screen, not the character. With this curse active, I couldn't even see the entire spell upgrade screen properly. The boss on the second floor drags the camera along when teleporting, which is disorienting and frustrating. For a roguelike, the lack of any meta-progression or difficulty options means that completing a run doesn't make the next one any easier. The only thing you gain is personal skill improvement. Combined with the relatively high difficulty, this makes the cycle of repeated deaths feel unrewarding and saps my motivation to keep trying. Localization Issues: Almost forgot—the classic "口口口" problem in Chinese localization. Missing commas between Chinese and English text also cause display errors. These are the issues I've encountered so far. I'll write more if I come across others. I'm supporting the developer's game, but it's hard to call this an outstanding title in its current state. It feels more like an unfinished product—hoping for improvements in future updates.

Giving this vote with a lot of nuance, simply because I think the current ratings are a bit high. Note that I haven't had the time to finish the game yet, but I've reached world 3 and from the achievements I'm guesstimating that I've probably seen the majority of the game's core mechanics. For its price, it's not bad. It's a relatively cookie-cutter modern roguelike. Builds feel shallow and META-oriented, because there's not that much synergy between components and the passive relics feel a bit underwhelming. On the positive side, the base mechanics feel well-established and enemy attack patterns are solid and mostly easy to understand. I like that every enemy doesn't constantly deal contact damage, opening up the close range that would be needlessly dangerous in most other games. The music is great as well. If you're considering buying the game because of the developer or without much prior roguelike experience, I wouldn't say it's a bad choice. Otherwise you might not find that much interesting to see.

I have some issues with this game. The first two ruining the enjoyment completely: 1) There's this "Anarchy" bonus stage in which you can get knowledge and relics if you survive for long enough. You can't opt out of the Glass Crutch if it finds you here and it makes you stuck on taking double damage for the rest of your run. I wish I could blacklist the item so it never appears again. 2) There's no brightness/gamma setting. The game is unplayable during the day if you have a window pouring sunshine into your room. 3) If you find a health pack and want to save it for later, you have to push it all the way back to the shopkeeper or run to the place where it dropped. Being able to grab it and teleport back would be nice. Even better if you could store it in place of one of your spells. Even if that meant out-of-combat use only. 4) There's no difficulty settings. Many would like to play this game on Easy, making checkpoints on every floor. Even if that disabled getting Steam achievements. Some would even prefer the game on Hard, with some negative relic being applied as a constant effect in return for more knowledge gained or some RNG control. If you aren't bothered by any of this, you'll probably enjoy the game. Edit: I now play the game only at night and play around the problematic items. Just skip any Anarchy stage content. The game is quite enjoyable now. There's also a problem if you have multiple screens, you have to care not to send your cursor over. Died to that "feature" too. I now have this free 3rd party "Windowed Borderless Gaming" software. It can lock the cursor to the game. You can still alt-tab to the other screen and the game won't minimize. I did experience some barrel missing a texture (was pure white) and had a game crash. Both happened only once in my 11h of gameplay. A crash is a bad way to end a run though. Did record it and will make a bug report. Hopefully much of this stuff gets fixed so I can recommend it. Edit2: Receive a free relic? Yes -> Permanent friggin' Glass Crutch not taking "no" for an answer! Edit3: Removing one negative point from the list. It used to say "You have no control over RNG in any way anywhere. Can't fix or even bump up the chances of your favourite spells or upgrades." Every spell that drops, drops only once. That means that you can use Knowledge (currency) sparingly until you get the spells you want and upgrade only them. Most spells are still either crap or overpowered, but at least you have some control over the RNG. The game is still getting updates which is a huge plus! Hopefully those issues above get addressed. I do want to leave a positive review and be honest about it.

As of the time of writing my review, I have 11hrs of gameplay and haven't beaten the game. This is a testament to how stupidly difficult this game is. I understand this is not the dev's main priority so I can sort of understand that the game is unpolished, but unless the game was made with the intention of being a troll game with it's difficulty then I CANNOT recommend this game even to the most die hard roguelike players. This game is difficult, enemies and bosses have little to almost no indications of attacking. It also doesn't help that the dodge roll feels like it works half the time or the timing window with invulnerability frames is too tight. Half the time I can perfectly dodge an enemy but other times, I get hit doing what feels like the same action. The game also suffers with its visuals, the camera initially following the camera makes it harder to see when your character is about to get hit. At least there is a setting to change this unlike the bloom in the game. The game's main environments are dark with little light but with the "blessing of the sun god" ability the game instantly becomes hard to see. But the main point is that the visuals along with how inconsistent they are, make it harder to see and play the game. Lastly, this game relies too much on RNG, most spells having upgrades that are more of a detriment than an "actual" upgrade. Also you cannot unequip relics which further debuffs you even though it is supposed to buff you like the "Bionic arm" (i think that's its name), it's main function is to push enemies away but it usually just leads to them being pushed in to the player. Otherwise most relics do too little or have major debuff like the Cooldown ring and obviously the "Glass Crutches" with only a +50% attack in return of taking 2x the damage. Even with all it's faults I will try and beat this game eventually. I like the game, it's somewhat fun trying to figure out the terribly designed mess to find some path to winning the game. But if this wasn't made from a Vtuber I love. I would not play this game nor would I even pay for this rushed game (I partially blame the Neuro community and Vedal) Anyway, 11/10 ABANDONED ARCHIVE IS GOTY 2025 !!!! BEST GAME EVER MADE !!!1! Edit: I have finally beaten the game after 22 hrs, my opinion remains the same, but with more advice. To anyone who may want to beat the game, you WILL need to go through the portal right before the final boss, it will loop you back to the beginning and you can attempt the final boss after how many loops. Ofc the enemies will get harder but it will be worth it to avoid most, well... mainly one bs attack from the final boss that fills the whole screen :) I didn't go through the portal initially because I thought this would lock me out of the final boss, thinking that it lead to an endless mode. Even though I have beaten the game, I will still try and 100%, because I like inflicting pain to myself. To end this edit, I will pull a quote from one of the greatest minds of all time: "This game sucks" -Neuro-sama

Big fan of Vedal/Neuro, but the game feels pretty unfinished. Many small annoyences, the difficulty is pretty unreasonable, all the upgrades you can get feel very disconnected from each other and are pretty meaningless, or at least I haven't found any combos, a map is desperately needed, and you can only get very few of these uprades before fighting the first bosses that all have like 2x the HP they should. Even after I got nice spell upgrades, I finally got to the 2nd floor, and the enemies got so much more HP that they took even longer to kill. I get the vision, I really do, but it neededs way more time to cook, which it probably won't get. More spells, more variety, serious rebalancing, more impactful items, fun item combos that make this type of game feel fun, just to name a few. Can't really recommend it in this state, though I guess the price also kinda reflects that. I will preface this with my playtime being low, so some points may be improved by further gameplay, and maybe at some point I'll do more and revise this. Unfortunately, the reason my playtime is low is because the game simply doesn't hook me as a roguelike thus far. Positive: -Variety of attacks and upgrades for them that make loadouts feel new. Even just playing a bit, I ran into many spells and upgrade paths. There's definitely some depth there. -There are a decent number of instances of decisionmaking in the field; spending money to reroll boons, taking chances on events that might give less than stellar outcomes, etc. The game doesn't feel like it's forcing me to make bad choices like some others fall into, which is nice. Negative: -In my opinion, the visuals are a big hurdle. A lot of the maps are very repetitive, the sprites and animations feel flat, and the spells are mostly functional but some leave a lot to be desired in terms of indicators. On top of that, the atmosphere of the game is *very* dark, and while dark aesthetics can work, here I find it mostly just makes the aforementioned bits feel worse. Especially because it gets [i]even darker[/i] when on low health. -The gameplay definitely wants to be a fast-paced dodgy game along the lines of Enter the Gungeon, but it feels like it misses the mark in a few regards. With animations not being very fluid, figuring out attack indicators and i-frames is quite difficult. Items that improve dodge rolls work in odd ways, slowing everything else down rather than actually speeding up your roll, which makes things difficult when trying to dodge fast attacks at certain angles. Time slow abilities are inconsistent when enemy projectiles are spawned at certain times. Despite stun being a very frequent mechanic, its helpfulness is varied, as some enemies follow through with their attacks during/after stun while others stop entirely; this issue in particular compounds with the speedy or nonexistent visual cues. Once you've fought a boss, you're locked into the room and forced to teleport to the next stage, meaning you can't switch up your loadout or refill HP before going to the next floor. Each of these is a relatively small gripe / nitpick, but they all came up in my limited time playing, and adding them all up leads to a game that felt hard for unsatisfying reasons rather than solely the player's lack of skill. -While in the positives I talked about in-field choices that felt good, having to teleport back to the start room to upgrade spells leads to two situations, both of which are negative to me. On the one hand, if you just get good enough at patterns and dodging, you don't need to upgrade spells much, but then it feels stagnant. On the other, you can go back to upgrade before finding a boss, but then you're doing a big walk back. If you haven't found the boss room yet, you're also required to then do a full walk back with no map or teleports. Overall: Given that I believe this is a first game project, I'd say it's decently above average and there's something there for people who want something simple, and probably much more content I haven't seen; particularly the story, which I didn't feel like I could comment on yet. Additionally, for anyone who wants to buy the game for its creator and connection to Neuro-sama, I wouldn't call it a waste of money, especially at its low pricepoint. That said, for people disconnected from that fandom and looking for something to put a ton of hours into, while I think these issues are fine to have in a first game and it's a point of improvement for future work, they also do mean that I'm going to say I don't really recommend it on its own merits as it stands. With a plethora of options on the market for roguelikes with spellslinging or fast paced high-execution gameplay, I think Abandoned Archive does fall a bit short on the list.
